summary:
Minetra is a web-based geospatial platform designed to explore mining landscape changes using multi-temporal L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations from NASA–ISRO's NISAR mission.

The platform processes NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) data, focusing on HH and HV backscatter measurements from different acquisition dates. Users can define an Area of Interest (AOI), compare temporal backscatter differences, explore seven-class Random Forest surface predictions, examine spatial statistics, and generate structured PDF reports.

Demonstrated over the Sangatta–Bengalon mining region in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, Minetra analyzed a 203.25 km² AOI containing  516.433 pixels across two observations separated by 132 days.

By integrating temporal radar analysis, thematic classification, and spatial reporting into one workflow, Minetra aims to make complex satellite observations more accessible and interpretable for Earth observation researchers, geospatial analysts, and environmental stakeholders.
details:
Project Overview

Minetra is an interactive geospatial platform developed to explore mining landscape changes through multi-temporal L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations. It addresses the challenge of transforming complex radar measurements into spatial information that can be explored and interpreted through an accessible analytical workflow.

How It Works

The platform uses NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) products. The current implementation focuses on HH and HV polarization measurements from two acquisition dates: June 20 and October 30, 2026.

The workflow consists of four main stages:

  1. Area of Interest Selection: Users define a geographic area within the available NISAR data coverage.
  2. Temporal Backscatter Analysis: The platform calculates pixel-level differences between observations to generate HH and HV backscatter change maps.
  3. Thematic Surface Classification: A Random Forest model uses four temporal polarization features (HH and HV from both dates) to predict seven thematic surface categories.
  4. Spatial Summarization and Reporting: The resulting maps, area statistics, and analytical information are organized into downloadable PDF reports.

Demonstration and Results

Minetra was demonstrated over a mining landscape in the Sangatta–Bengalon region of East Kalimantan, Indonesia.

The selected demonstration area covered 203.12 km² and contained 516.433 valid pixels. The two NISAR observations were separated by 132 days. The mean backscatter differences across the selected AOI were approximately −1.29 dB for HH and −1.39 dB for HV.

These outputs demonstrate how multi-temporal radar measurements can be compared and summarized to investigate spatial variations in a changing mining landscape.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Minetra brings several analytical components together in one platform, reducing the need to navigate separate processing tools and manually assemble analytical outputs.

Its intended benefits include:

  • Making multi-temporal SAR analysis more accessible to geospatial researchers and learners.
  • Providing spatial visualization of radar backscatter changes.
  • Offering additional thematic context through machine-learning-based surface predictions.
  • Supporting quantitative exploration through AOI statistics.
  • Improving the communication and documentation of analytical results through automated reporting.

Minetra is intended as an exploratory research and geospatial analysis platform, not as an automated system for determining mining legality or identifying the cause of every observed surface change.

Technology and Tools

The project combines geospatial data processing, machine learning, and web application development.

The implementation uses Python-based backend processing, a TypeScript-based frontend, geospatial raster analysis, HDF5 data handling, and a Random Forest classification workflow.

The platform integrates spatial visualization, analytical processing, and PDF report generation into a single application.

Creativity and Innovation

Minetra's approach focuses on integrating temporal L-band radar analysis and thematic surface exploration into an AOI-based workflow.

Rather than presenting isolated satellite images, the platform combines backscatter differences, model-predicted surface categories, quantitative spatial summaries, and structured reports. This creates multiple complementary perspectives for exploring mining landscape changes.

Future Development

Future development will focus on expanding geographical coverage, incorporating additional NISAR observation dates, improving classification through stronger reference data and independent validation, and exploring interferometric SAR products for surface deformation studies.

The long-term vision is to make satellite radar observations easier to explore, interpret, and communicate for a wider geospatial community.
